subject: Agriculture
title: Egypt and the Nile
description: A quick win: understand Egypt and the Nile.

hook.text: Every year, the Nile flooded. Egyptians didn't fight it—they built their entire farming system around it.

buildup.text: Floodwaters deposited rich black silt across the valley. Farmers planted directly into this natural fertilizer.

discovery.text: Egypt developed basin irrigation—walled fields that trapped floodwater and slowly released it to crops.

twist.text: If the flood was too high, villages drowned. Too low, and famine followed. Life depended on the river's mood.

climax.text: This system fed Egypt for 5,000 years—until the Aswan Dam ended the annual flood in 1970.

punchline.text: Egypt was the gift of the Nile—and its hostage.

quiz.question: What made the Nile's annual flood beneficial for Egyptian farming?
options: It deposited rich silt that acted as natural fertilizer
